chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Faqih al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. al-Husayn from Muhammad b. Jumhur, and from Muhammad b. Ziyad, from one who heard Muhammad b. Muslim al-Thaqafi say: I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them) say:

Indeed, Allah the Exalted has angels assigned to the fasting people. They seek forgiveness for them every day of the month of Ramadan until its end. They call to the fasting people every night at the time of their breaking of fast: 'Rejoice, O servants of Allah! You have hungered a little and you will be satiated much. You are blessed, and blessing be upon you.' Until, on the last night of the month of Ramadan, they call to them: 'Rejoice, O servants of Allah! Allah has forgiven your sins and accepted your repentance. So see how you will be when you start anew.'

key_terms.أبشروا: Rejoice — an imperative of glad tidings, often used by angels in Islamic texts
key_terms.تستأنفون: You start anew — the word implies beginning afresh after the forgiveness of Ramadan
key_terms.ملائكة موكلين: Angels specifically assigned and charged with a duty — here, watching over those who fast

ai.seo_question: What role do angels play during Ramadan for those who fast?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (as), narrated at the first Ramadan assembly in 367 AH, reveals the unseen spiritual dimension of fasting. Angels are specifically assigned to those who fast during Ramadan, interceding for them daily and proclaiming glad tidings each night at the time of iftar. The concluding warning about what comes after Ramadan underscores that forgiveness is a fresh start requiring continued effort.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Faqih al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father (rh) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad b. al-Husayn from Muhammad b. Jamhur, and from Muhammad b. Ziyad from one who heard Muhammad b. Muslim al-Thaqafi say:  I heard Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as) say:

For Allah, there are angels assigned to those who fast. They seek repentance for them every day in the month of Ramadan until its end. They call to those who fast every night at the time of their breakfast: “Rejoice, servants of Allah, for you have hungered little and will be satiated much. You will be blessed, and blessing will come by you” – until the end of the night in the month of Ramadan, wherein they will call to them: “Rejoice, servants of Allah, for Allah has forgiven your sins and accepted your repentance. So, see how you will be when you continue.”
